signals.evidence: MeterReadingScreen.handleSubmit always calls addToQueue() instead of a direct apiRequest, and alerts the user with t('meters.submitSuccess') when isConnected is true (line 144-147). useOfflineSupport.processQueue is only triggered on NetInfo reconnect transitions (hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:593-619) or via SyncProgressToast manual retry — never when adding to the queue — so a reading submitted while online sits in AsyncStorage indefinitely.
signals.failure_scenario: User opens app with working connectivity, taps a water meter reading, enters a value, taps Submit. Alert pops up 'Reading submitted successfully' and the pending card shows status='syncing'. The device never disconnects, so NetInfo never fires a true→true transition. POST /api/v1/meter-readings never happens. The utility billing cycle closes without the reading; user is billed on an estimate while believing they filed it.

signals.evidence: NFCCredentialManager.apiRequest sets only `Content-Type` and `Authorization` headers; it omits `X-Tenant-ID` that useApi.ts:63-72 explicitly documents is required by RlsConnection-extracted api-server routes. All NFC endpoints (/api/v1/access/credentials, /invitations, /log, /revoke-all) are called through this method.
signals.failure_scenario: A multi-org manager logs into tenant A, enrolls NFC credentials, logs out, logs back in to tenant B. On tenant B, fetchCredentials() POSTs /api/v1/access/credentials with no X-Tenant-ID: the RLS extractor either 403s (NFC door access broken) or — worse, if the backend falls back to the JWT tenant_id elsewhere while the local cache still holds the previous tenant's manifest — serves/stores cross-tenant credentials.

signals.evidence: useEffect at line 37-48 awaits bridge.isWidgetSupported() then bridge.getAllConfigs() and calls setIsSupported/setConfigs/setIsLoading unconditionally — no cancelled flag, no cleanup. handleRefreshAll (line 75-80) has the same shape with setIsLoading after an awaited bridge.updateAllWidgets().
signals.failure_scenario: On a slow device (iOS 14 initial WidgetKit cold load, several hundred ms), user taps Dashboard→Widget Settings and immediately taps back. checkSupport() resolves after unmount and calls setIsSupported(true) + setConfigs(savedConfigs) + setIsLoading(false) on an unmounted component — fires 'Can't perform a React state update on an unmounted component' warning in dev and leaks the bridge closure until GC.
